decisions.question: How are the phase's deliverables split into at most 7 tasks, and do the structure-set polish items routed to this phase get a task?

options.label: seven tasks, polish as Task 6
options.consequence: fixture library and schemas; PENDING and the report; the schema set; the surface and reject sets; the async shell; structure-set polish; gate and verification doc. Each task can be rejected by a reviewer on its own; the cap is reached

options.label: six tasks, polish left routed
options.consequence: a smaller review sitting; the range-typo hang and the covers-reading defects wait for nidana.model.6 or .7

options.label: fold the polish into the shell task
options.consequence: one task fewer, but a task mixing unrelated rules that a reviewer cannot reject separately

decisions.chosen: seven tasks, polish as Task 6
decisions.why: The derivative allows 7 tasks. Each polish item is a few lines in files no other task touches (ids.dart, contract.dart, structure.dart), and the eager range expansion is a hang every gate is exposed to. Order puts the report before the schema set so that every new cli test is written once against the final summary form. The signal that would have changed this: nidana.model.1's 9x overrun repeating in review, in which case Task 6 is the one to defer.

decisions.question: Which files hold the new pure core, and where does lib/fixture.dart find the workspace root?

options.label: one file per set plus shared readers
options.consequence: lib/src/json_document.dart, packages.dart, schema.dart, analysis.dart, surface.dart, reject.dart; fixture.dart imports shell.dart's findWorkspaceRoot, so the root is defined once

options.label: one file for both analyzed sets
options.consequence: fewer files; surface and reject change together although their rules differ

options.label: fixture.dart with its own root search
options.consequence: no import of the shell from the public library, but two definitions of the workspace root that can drift

decisions.chosen: one file per set plus shared readers
decisions.why: nidana.model.1 names each set's file after the set (structure.dart) and keeps readers separate; nidana.model.6 and .7 will add behavior and file/cli files beside these. ADR-001 and topology-ir@v1 define the root identically for the tool and for expectMatchesSchema, so one function serves both.

decisions.question: How does the schema set receive the schema file and the documents, and is a document that is not UTF-8 a fixture defect or an environment error (routed item: invalid UTF-8 is a fixture defect)?

options.label: bytes in the snapshot, decoded by the pure core
options.consequence: SlugSnapshot.schemaBytes replaces hasSchemaFile (kept as a getter) and documents holds each valid/ and invalid/ file's bytes; a non-UTF-8 document is FAIL document, exit 1; the structure set's Dart sources are untouched

options.label: strings read by the shell
options.consequence: readAsStringSync throws on invalid UTF-8, so the replay exits 2 naming the file: the routed defect stays

options.label: a sealed content type for every file
options.consequence: fixes Dart sources too, but changes the structure set's input and its tests in this phase

decisions.chosen: bytes in the snapshot, decoded by the pure core
decisions.why: It makes invalid UTF-8 a fixture defect for the set this phase lands at the cost of two snapshot fields. Dart sources stay as nidana.model.1 reads them: a non-UTF-8 Dart fixture still fails loudly (exit 2 naming the file), so nothing passes unseen; that part stays routed.

decisions.question: Which fixtures does the schema set report, and what happens to the documents when the schema file is absent or does not compile?

options.label: the schema file is a fixture; documents only when it compiles
options.consequence: PASS or FAIL schema hsdd/contract/schema/{slug}.schema.json first; a missing or broken schema is its only line (exit 1); the committed gate replays 46 and 58 schema fixtures

options.label: documents only, a broken schema as an environment error
options.consequence: a contract defect would exit 2 as if the machine were broken

options.label: every document fails with schema unavailable
options.consequence: dozens of lines repeating one defect

decisions.chosen: the schema file is a fixture; documents only when it compiles
decisions.why: An absent or uncompilable schema is a defect of the contract's fixtures (ADR-001 item 8), so it fails like a fixture; judging documents against no schema says nothing. A schema that is a JSON string, array or null does not compile, because JsonSchema.create would decode a string a second time.

decisions.question: Which files below valid/ and invalid/ does the schema set judge?

options.label: every file, recursively, hidden ones excluded
options.consequence: a non-JSON or non-.json file fails as a document instead of going unreplayed

options.label: .json files directly in the directory
options.consequence: the prototype's choice; a nested or misnamed case is silently skipped

options.label: .json files recursively
options.consequence: a misnamed case is silently skipped

decisions.chosen: every file, recursively, hidden ones excluded
decisions.why: ADR-001 item 5 says every valid/ file validates and no invalid/ file does; a file the set skips would be a case nobody replays. Both committed trees hold only .json files directly in the directory, so the stricter reading changes no committed result.

decisions.question: Routed: does setsOf follow the structure set's rule that a schema covers clause counts only when the schema file exists?

options.label: keep setsOf; the set fails at the schema path
options.consequence: a slug with valid/ or invalid/ and no schema file runs the schema set, which prints FAIL schema-file (absent), exit 1

options.label: setsOf requires the schema file
options.consequence: such a slug would not run the set at all; only the structure set's covers-clause check would notice, and only when the contract has a covers clause

decisions.chosen: keep setsOf; the set fails at the schema path
decisions.why: A half-present schema set must fail loudly. ADR-001 item 9 gives a slug every set it has, and a slug with valid/ has the schema set; the structure set's rule decides coverage, not whether a set runs.
evidence: docs/auto-run/impl-execution-plan.md Routed to later phases (S101 final fix wave)

decisions.question: Routed: does a structure failure suppress a slug's other sets?

options.label: no: every planned set runs
options.consequence: each set judges its own fixtures; a structure failure and, say, a schema failure both print

options.label: yes: skip the slug's other sets
options.consequence: fewer lines, but independent defects hide behind an unrelated structure finding

decisions.chosen: no: every planned set runs
decisions.why: ADR-001 item 9 says structure runs first, not that it gates the others; the exit code is 1 either way. The reject set ignores malformed markers that structure reports, so the two never contradict each other; reporting both only adds information.

decisions.question: Routed: how many dart analyze processes does one replay start?

options.label: one per replay over every non-pending surface and reject library, none when there is none
options.consequence: one process for --all; the shell reads every snapshot first and prints after; zero targets start nothing

options.label: one per slug and set
options.consequence: up to 18 analyzer starts for --all

options.label: one per fixture
options.consequence: 65 starts over the committed tree

decisions.chosen: one per replay over every non-pending surface and reject library, none when there is none
decisions.why: One dart analyze takes many file paths and analyzes all 65 committed libraries in about 0.4 s; batching costs only printing after the analysis. dart analyze without a path analyzes the working directory, so zero targets must start nothing.

decisions.question: How are the analyzer's reported paths matched to fixtures, and what if a reported path matches none?

options.label: map normalized and symlink-resolved target paths; a stray is an environment error
options.consequence: works under macOS's /var to /private/var temp paths and a linked checkout; a mismatch exits 2 instead of passing a surface library

options.label: compare normalized paths only
options.consequence: every diagnostic is dropped when the root is reached through a link, so surface libraries pass vacuously

options.label: drop strays silently
options.consequence: an attribution bug passes surface libraries

decisions.chosen: map normalized and symlink-resolved target paths; a stray is an environment error
decisions.why: dart analyze reports symlink-resolved paths whatever form it was given, and only the analyzed files' diagnostics; so a stray can only be an attribution bug, which must not read as a pass.

decisions.question: How does the reject set compare the reported (line, code) pairs with the markers' pairs, and how does it report a difference?

options.label: set semantics with missing and unexpected problems
options.consequence: the pairs form sets; missing-diagnostic 'line {n}: {code}, named by the marker on line {n-1}, not reported', unexpected-diagnostic with severity, code and message; marker 'no // expect-diagnostic: marker' first; line by line, missing before unexpected; malformed markers name nothing

options.label: multiset semantics
options.consequence: a code reported twice on its line would need two markers, which item 4's one-marker-per-line form cannot write

options.label: one mismatch problem listing both sets
options.consequence: harder to read which marker is wrong

decisions.chosen: set semantics with missing and unexpected problems
decisions.why: ADR-001 item 4 speaks of pairs equal to the markers' pairs, and the prototypes that confirmed every committed reject code compared sets. The phase's Verification (a marker on the wrong line, a wrong code, an extra warning) maps onto these two problem kinds.

decisions.question: Which analyze command does the tool run, and what does a surface failure print?

options.label: analyze --fatal-infos --format=json with absolute paths; one problem per diagnostic
options.consequence: the command item 4 names; detail 'line {n}: {SEVERITY} {code}: {message}', sorted by line

options.label: analyze --format=json without --fatal-infos
options.consequence: identical report, a command that reads differently from item 4

options.label: codes only
options.consequence: shorter lines a reader has to look up

decisions.chosen: analyze --fatal-infos --format=json with absolute paths; one problem per diagnostic
decisions.why: --fatal-infos changes only the exit code, which the tool never reads (it reads the JSON), so passing it costs nothing and keeps the command item 4's. The message tells the reader what to fix.

decisions.question: What makes a fixture PENDING in this phase, and does PENDING detection already cover behavior libraries?

options.label: package: URIs of imports and exports; surface and reject now, behavior at nidana.model.6
options.consequence: Pending(path, packages) for a surface or reject library naming a package absent from .dart_tool/package_config.json; the behavior set stays not implemented and will reuse absentPackages

options.label: imports only
options.consequence: an export of an absent package would fail as uri_does_not_exist, a defect

options.label: mark behavior libraries PENDING now
options.consequence: outcomes for a set this version cannot run

decisions.chosen: package: URIs of imports and exports; surface and reject now, behavior at nidana.model.6
decisions.why: ADR-001 item 9 says a fixture that names a package absent from the package configuration is PENDING; an export names a package as surely as an import. The behavior set lands at nidana.model.6 (D1), which applies the same function to bindings.

decisions.question: Routed: how does the summary line show PENDING fixtures?

options.label: always '{n} fixtures: {p} passed, {f} failed, {q} pending'
options.consequence: one form; 'fixture' for one; nidana.model.1's tests change their expected summaries

options.label: the pending count only when non-zero
options.consequence: two forms of the line

options.label: summary unchanged
options.consequence: PENDING fixtures counted nowhere

decisions.chosen: always '{n} fixtures: {p} passed, {f} failed, {q} pending'
decisions.why: One form is easier to read and to grep in a gate log; it also fixes the routed '1 fixtures'.

decisions.question: Routed: how does an environment error carry a message in place of SetUnavailable's fixed text?

options.label: SetUnavailable gains a reason
options.consequence: ERROR {set} {slug}: {reason}; notImplemented(set) keeps nidana.model.1's text for behavior, file and cli; reasons for a missing or malformed package configuration, a dart that cannot start, no JSON report, a stray path

options.label: a new sealed variant beside SetUnavailable
options.consequence: two variants with the same meaning and exit code

options.label: a replay-wide environment error that aborts
options.consequence: other slugs' sets would not report

decisions.chosen: SetUnavailable gains a reason
decisions.why: SetUnavailable already means 'this set could not run' and already outranks failures in exitCodeOf; a field keeps one variant and lets the rest of the replay report.

decisions.question: When has dart analyze failed to run, and how do the tests reach those paths?

options.label: no JSON report or a ProcessException; runCli takes an optional dart
options.consequence: the exit code is never read; tests call runCli in process with a missing path and with /bin/echo

options.label: an exit code above 3
options.consequence: relies on undocumented codes; a crash that prints JSON-less output with code 3 would read as a clean report

options.label: no seam
options.consequence: the environment-error paths of the analysis go untested

decisions.chosen: no JSON report or a ProcessException; runCli takes an optional dart
decisions.why: The report's presence, not the exit code, says whether the analysis ran (A5 shows exit codes 0 to 3 with a full report, A6 exit 64 with none). The parameter defaults to Platform.resolvedExecutable, so the bin script and ADR-001 item 9's 'dart running the tool' are unchanged.

decisions.question: How does expectMatchesSchema fail, what does it print, and does it cache compiled schemas?

options.label: TestFailure for validation errors, StateError for root and schema problems, no cache
options.consequence: 'does not match {path}:' and one line per json_schema error; a missing root, a missing schema or a schema that does not compile is an error, not a failure

options.label: TestFailure for everything
options.consequence: a broken fixture reads like the producer's failure

options.label: cache compiled schemas
options.consequence: mutable global state for a few milliseconds per call

decisions.chosen: TestFailure for validation errors, StateError for root and schema problems, no cache
decisions.why: topology-ir@v1 fixes the failure for validation errors only; the split mirrors the tool's fixture failure versus environment error. The owner prefers immutability, and seven sample graphs compile quickly.

decisions.question: What temporary workspace do the analyzer-backed tests seed, and how is it resolved?

options.label: a pub workspace with a dependency-free stand-in, resolved by Platform.resolvedExecutable pub get --offline
options.consequence: packages/sample with final class Sample; the committed fixtures' analysis options copied in; no hosted package needed; about 0.1 s to resolve

options.label: fixtures analyzed inside the repository
options.consequence: writes under hsdd/ or analyzes against the root's resolution, which holds no stand-in

options.label: a stand-in with hosted dependencies from the cache
options.consequence: slower and nothing the sets need

decisions.chosen: a pub workspace with a dependency-free stand-in, resolved by Platform.resolvedExecutable pub get --offline
decisions.why: fvm runs no dart in a temp directory, so the SDK dart must be called directly; the stand-in's diagnostics for every seed were captured exactly; the repository's bin script resolves its own packages from such a workspace. A workspace without the stand-in is the 'producer absent' case of the phase's Verification.

decisions.question: When is .dart_tool/package_config.json read, and what if it is missing or malformed?

options.label: only when surface or reject is planned; missing or malformed is their SetUnavailable reason
options.consequence: structure and schema replays need no resolution; a broken environment exits 2 naming the file

options.label: always, as a replay-wide environment error
options.consequence: the structure-only gate would depend on resolution it does not use

options.label: treat every package as absent
options.consequence: every fixture PENDING, exit 1, reading like an absent producer

decisions.chosen: only when surface or reject is planned; missing or malformed is their SetUnavailable reason
decisions.why: PENDING must mean a producer is absent, not that resolution is broken.

decisions.question: How are the routed structure-set polish items fixed?

options.label: bounded ranges, right-trimmed lines, unclosed covers bullets, raw Case cells, ranges in formatIds
options.consequence: a range spanning 1000 or more ids is no list (malformed, reported at once); every contract line right-trimmed; a - schema: or - file: bullet holding 'covers ' without the closing clause is a validation-form failure; the Case cell kept as written; runs of three or more ids print as G{a} to G{b}; continuation lines not joined

options.label: symbolic ranges checked against the declared ids
options.consequence: exact unknown-id messages for huge ranges, but new id types through contract.dart, dart_library.dart and structure.dart

options.label: join indented continuation lines into their bullet
options.consequence: a small markdown parser in the reader

decisions.chosen: bounded ranges, right-trimmed lines, unclosed covers bullets, raw Case cells, ranges in formatIds
decisions.why: Each fix is a few lines, and every committed contract reads as before (no Validation line ends in whitespace; both committed bullets holding 'covers ' end with the clause). A wrapped bullet now fails loudly (unclosed covers or names-no-node), and every committed Validation bullet is one line, so joining continuation lines buys nothing today.

decisions.question: Routed: what do --all with no slug directory, and a symbolic link where a slug directory belongs, do?

options.label: exit 2 with an error line
options.consequence: 'error: no slug directory under hsdd/contract/fixture/'; a link raises FileSystemException("a slug's fixture directory is a symbolic link", path), which runCli already prints and exits 2 on

options.label: follow a linked slug directory
options.consequence: a fixture tree outside hsdd/contract/fixture/ joins the replay

options.label: keep nidana.model.1's behavior
options.consequence: 0 fixtures and exit 0, or a slug silently skipped

decisions.chosen: exit 2 with an error line
decisions.why: Both are broken workspaces, and a gate must not pass on them. nidana.model.1's link policy already treats links in a slug as files; a linked slug is outside what ADR-001 item 2 locates.

decisions.question: How does a test show that diagnostics reach their fixtures when the workspace root is reached through a symbolic link?

options.label: call runCli in process with the linked root
options.consequence: the shell sees the unresolved root and must map the analyzer's resolved paths

options.label: run the bin script with the link as working directory
options.consequence: the child reads its working directory back resolved, so the test would pass without exercising the mapping

decisions.chosen: call runCli in process with the linked root
decisions.why: Settled by experiment X2 during self-review: a process started through a linked working directory reads Directory.current resolved.

experiments.question: What does dart analyze --format=json print for fixtures under hsdd/contract/fixture/analysis_options.yaml (several paths, symlinked temp paths, committed fixtures by path, exit codes, failures)? Can a temp workspace with a stand-in be resolved offline, and with which dart? Which dart runs the tool and its tests, and what cwd does a child started through a link read? How does package:json_schema 5.2.2 report errors and compile failures, and do the committed schema sets pass? How does package_config parse? Does IOOverrides change Directory.current?
experiments.finding: W0: fvm dart in a temp dir runs no dart (exit 127). W1: Platform.resolvedExecutable pub get --offline resolves a dependency-free stand-in workspace in 0.1 s. A1: one analyze takes several file paths; stdout is the JSON document alone; diagnostics carry code, severity (ERROR/WARNING/INFO), location.file, location.range.start.line (1-based), problemMessage; a library a fixture imports is not reported. A2: identical JSON with --fatal-infos. A3: reported paths are symlink-resolved (/private/var). A5: exits 0/2/3, 1 only for infos under --fatal-infos. A6: a missing path exits 64 with usage on stderr, empty stdout. A7: a bad fixture options key is not reported. A8, A9: the root's hsdd/** exclusion does not stop analysis by path; the committed fixtures report uri_does_not_exist today. A10: 65 committed libraries in about 0.4 s. A11: exact codes, lines and messages of the plan's seeds against final class Sample. A12: the repo's bin script resolves its packages from a temp workspace with its own package config. X1: resolvedExecutable is the SDK dart under fvm dart run and fvm dart test. X2: a child started through a linked cwd reads it resolved. J1/M: validate reports every error, toString '{path or # (root)}: {message}', a missing required property reported twice. J2: create throws FormatException or ArgumentError. J5: format is an annotation. J6: topology-ir 45/45 and topic-codegen 57/57 documents judged correctly. P: parseString does no I/O, malformed input raises PackageConfigFormatException or goes to onError. O: IOOverrides works; matcher's fail throws TestFailure.
